title: Private Deployments: VPC & On-Prem Reference, Day-2 Ops, Upgrade and Rollback Procedures
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary

This document is the canonical reference for Redwood Inference private deployment customers and engineers implementing VPC and on-prem deployments. It consolidates: reference architectures, on-prem packaging guidelines, a customer requirements library, day-2 operational procedures, and detailed upgrade and rollback playbooks. Use this as the single source of truth for planning, executing, and operating Private deployments.

Scope

- Covered: AWS/GCP/Azure VPC-based private deployments, air-gapped on-prem packaging, typical day-2 operations, formal upgrade and rollback procedures, and customer requirements mapping.
- Not covered: hosted API onboarding (see product-docs), Dedicated reserved-capacity ops.

Audience

- Solutions engineers, SREs, platform engineers, and customer technical leads.

Prerequisites and Customer Requirements (Quick checklist)

Before starting deployment, confirm the following with the customer. This table is a minimal requirements library — adapt per customer risk profile.

| Category | Requirement | Example / Notes | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| Networking | VPC with private subnets and NAT / egress rules | /24 CIDR blocks; BGP where required | Customer network team |
| IPingress | Static IPs or NAT gateway for control-plane egress | Required for license and metrics endpoints | Customer network team |
| DNS & Certificates | Private DNS zone + wildcard certs (TLS1.2+) or ACM | Ensure wildcard CN matching *.redwood.local for internal routes | Customer ops / Redwood SE |
| Storage | NFS/SMB or cloud-backed PVCs with IOPS requirements | 2 TB baseline, provisioned IOPS for model artifacts | Customer infra |
| KMS / Secrets | Customer-managed KMS (optional) | HSM-backed keys for FIPS environments | Security / Customer |
| Identity | SSO / OIDC integration or SAML for console access | Role mappings documented in appendix | Customer IAM |
| Hardware | GPU nodes (NVIDIA A100/A30 or equivalent) or CPU fallback | Minimum 2 GPU nodes for HA; sizing guidance below | Customer infra |
| Compliance | Data residency and audit requirements | Retention windows, logging destinations | Legal / Security |

Reference Architectures (High level)

1) VPC-Hosted Private Control Plane with Customer Data Plane

- Control plane components (management, metrics ingestion, config API) run in Redwood-managed, customer-facing control endpoints via private peering or Transit Gateway.
- Data plane (model serving) runs in the customer VPC across private subnets on GPU instances.
- Recommended availability: 3 AZs; minimum 2 AZs for cost-constrained customers.

2) Fully Isolated On-Prem (Air Gapped)

- All components packaged as container images and install artifacts (RPM/DEB) delivered via secure media.
- Local artifact registry and local KMS/HSM optional.
- Optional outbound-only telemetry bridge via customer proxy for aggregated usage reporting.

3) Hybrid (Control plane SaaS, Data plane On-Prem)

- Best for customers who require minimal control-plane responsibilities but keep all inference on-prem for residency.

Packaging and Installation Notes

- Packaging formats supported: Helm charts (K8s), Debian/RPM bundles for non-K8s, and air-gap tarball with manifests.
- Helm values are parameterized for: image registry, node selectors, GPU resource requests, PVC classes, certs, and feature flags (KV cache, batching).
- Minimum Kubernetes version: 1.24+. CRI: containerd recommended.

Example installation command (Kubernetes, Helm):

1. Add registry and pull images to private registry (air-gap):
   - docker pull registry.redwood.ai/ri-serving:stable-2027-02-01
   - docker tag ... && docker push private.registry.company/ri-serving:stable-2027-02-01
2. Install with values.yaml:
   - helm upgrade --install redwood-serving ./charts/redwood \
       -f values.customer.yaml --namespace redwood --create-namespace

Day-2 Ops: Routine Procedures

- Daily checks (automated):
  - Control plane health endpoints: /healthz (3m window)
  - Model-serving process level: GPU utilization, KV-cache hit rate, request latencies P50/P95/P99
  - Disk usage on model artifact volumes (>80% alert)
- Weekly: dependency updates, cert rotations (see cert rotation playbook), backup verification (etcd / Postgres snapshots).
- Monthly: capacity planning review and autoscaler tuning.

Operational Runbook (common tasks)

1) Add a new model version to on-prem cluster
   1. Push model artifact to PVC or preloaded path.
   2. Update Model CRD: apiVersion: models.redwood.ai/v1, kind: ModelVersion, spec: {image, weightsPath, config}.
   3. Monitor rollout: kubectl get rollout model/<name> -w
   4. Validate: run canonical eval prompts and verify metrics in the console.

2) Replace a failed GPU node
   1. Cordon node: kubectl cordon <node>
   2. Drain workloads with grace period 60s: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
   3. Provision replacement hardware or schedule live migration to spare node.

Upgrade and Rollback Procedures (Formal Playbook)

Principles:
- Always run upgrades in a canary -> staged -> full rollout pattern.
- Maintain a tested rollback artifact set and automated verification tests for each stage.
- Nightly snapshots before upgrade (etcd, DBs, model artifact indexes).

Pre-upgrade checklist:
- Backups validated within last 24 hours (etcd/snapshots).
- Health baseline captured (latency, error rate, throughput).
- Sufficient spare capacity (20% headroom) for rolling upgrades.
- Stakeholders (SE, SRE, Customer) on standby window.

Canary upgrade steps (Kubernetes Helm example):
1. Create canary values: values.canary=true, replicaCount=1 per AZ.
2. helm upgrade --install redwood-serving ./charts/redwood -f values.canary.yaml --namespace redwood
3. Wait for canary health window (30-60 mins). Run smoke tests: /health, tokenized request flows, sample evals.
4. If green, promote to staged (10-25% of fleet) using horizontal rollout labels.
5. Monitor telemetry (latency P95, error rate) for 2x baseline window before full rollout.

Rollback criteria (any one of):
- P95 latency increases >40% from baseline for 10m window.
- Error rate >2% absolute (or >3x baseline) for 10m window.
- Canary fails startup or readiness probes.

Automated rollback (recommended):
- If Canary fails health gates, run: helm rollback redwood-serving <previous-revision> --namespace redwood
- For partial/staged rollbacks, use labels to target affected nodes and revert only updated replicas.

Manual rollback steps (if automation fails):
1. Revert manifests to previous git tag and reapply: kubectl apply -f manifests/v<X>.yaml
2. Force restart deployment and block new traffic via ingress weight shifting (see traffic routing below).
3. Verify baseline metrics restored before re-opening 100% traffic.

Traffic routing and graceful degradations

- We rely on ingress/edge (NGINX/Envoy) weights for traffic shifting. Typical rollout increments: 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 15-30 minute observation windows.
- Fallback policies: when a region loses capacity, requests route to secondary region variant with quantized model (smaller vRAM footprint) to preserve latency SLOs.

Verification and Post-Upgrade Validation

- Smoke tests: run 50 canonical prompts (from eval harness) and validate response tokens, latency P95 < baseline + 20%, and no functional regressions.
- Functional tests: targeted model QA (syntactic correctness, hallucination rates) run on representative prompt sets.
- Post-mortem window: capture metrics for 24-72 hours and flag regressions to applied-ml-and-evals.

Common Troubleshooting Notes

- Readiness/CrashLoopBackOff after upgrade: check init containers for model download timeouts. Increase pullPolicy or pre-warm artifacts.
- High latency after deploy: confirm batch sizes and batching daemon is running; check kernel selection logs under /var/log/redwood/kernel-sel.log.
- KV cache warmup: expect initial spike in tail latency until KV hit rate >70%. Consider pre-warming strategy during maintenance window.

Ownership and Contacts

- Deployment Owner: eng-private-deployments (primary contact on Slack #private-deployments).
- Oncall (SRE): rotation listed in eng-sre/runbooks. Engage via PagerDuty: Redwood-PrivateProd.
- Sales/SE escalation: contact assigned Solutions Engineer on account for access and permissions.

Appendix A: Sizing Guidance (example)

- Small proof-of-concept: 2x GPU nodes (A10/A30), 4vCPU control-plane, 500GB model storage.
- Production (3 AZs): 6-12 GPU nodes (A100), 2x control-plane replicas, 10 TB model storage with 3x replication.

Appendix B: Recommended Health SLOs

- P95 token latency: <350ms (interactive workloads)
- Availability (control plane): 99.95% monthly
- Model load success rate: 99.9%
